registrazione.premessa: It is only needed to save your patterns and to stop other people editing them. Browsing, opening and downloading requires no account.
registrazione.dati.password: The password is not kept. The server holds only a fingerprint of it, computed so that it cannot be reversed: not even whoever administers the service can read it back.
registrazione.dati.risposta: The same goes for the answer to the recovery question. The question itself stays readable, because it has to be shown to you.
registrazione.dati.recupero: There is no email and no other channel. If you forget the password, the only way back in is the answer to your recovery question. Choose one you will still know in a year and that nobody else could guess.

prodotto.paginaTitolo: Pattern Editor SVG — one cell, endless times
prodotto.sottotitolo: You draw a small square, about this big. The rest — the motif that covers a wall, a section, a whole technical drawing — comes by itself.
prodotto.cellaGuida: A cell with its own measurements, and inside it the shapes you want. The SVG document that comes out repeats it endlessly: the motif is not drawn, it is calculated — and it weighs as much as the cell, not as much as the wall it covers.
prodotto.tipiGuida: Rectangle, circle, ellipse, line, path, polygon, polyline, text, image. Each one is an extension of its own: the tenth is added without touching a line of the ones already there.
prodotto.tipo.rect: The brick of almost every motif: fills, bands, masonry textures.
prodotto.tipo.circle: Dots, bubbles, nail heads. When you need a shape without a direction.
prodotto.tipo.ellipse: A circle with a direction: scales, leaves, flattened pebbles.
prodotto.tipo.line: Technical hatching. Two points, and the motif comes from the repetition.
prodotto.tipo.path: Any profile: curves, arcs, outlines the other types cannot make.
prodotto.tipo.polygon: A closed polyline: hexagons, stars, tiles that fit together.
prodotto.tipo.polyline: An open polyline: zigzags, roof profiles, trends.
prodotto.tipo.text: Letters and numbers inside the motif: codes, dimensions, watermarks.
prodotto.tipo.image: A photograph or a raster drawing embedded in the cell.

vetrina.convertiTitolo: Opens a raster image (PNG, JPEG…) and tries to rebuild its motif with vector shapes
gestione.converti.illeggibile: The image could not be read: {0}
confronto.legenda: red: drawing that is missing · blue: drawing that was added
vetrina.coloriTitolo: How many colour bands to read the image as. Fewer give a cleaner drawing with fewer elements; more follow the image closely but produce a pattern that is hard to edit.
confronto.riprova: Change this and the image is converted again, without picking the file twice.
confronto.fedeltaTitolo: Normal: a few hundred shapes, a pattern you can still edit by hand. Maximum: corrections carry on until little is left over — still all vector, so still sharp at any scale, but thousands of elements. Tracing copy: the light vector drawing with an image on top carrying everything it could not render. It matches almost exactly and stops being a drawing — that part does not scale and cannot be edited.

prodotto.originiTitolo: You do not have to draw it from scratch
prodotto.originiGuida: A cell is composed shape by shape, and often that is the right way. But if the drawing you need already exists — in a file, or in a photograph — you can start from there.
prodotto.importaTesto: A drawing made with Illustrator, Inkscape or Figma becomes a pattern: the shapes come in one by one, with their colours, and the cell is read from the document's viewBox.
prodotto.importaNota: Before the editor opens it tells you what came in and what did not, and why. Nothing is saved until you confirm it.
prodotto.convertiTitolo: From a photograph to a vector pattern
prodotto.convertiTesto: Load the image of a floor, a hatch, any texture at all: the tool looks for how often the drawing repeats, reduces it to a few tints, and rebuilds the tile with real rectangles and polygons — not a pixel tracing, shapes you can open and edit.
prodotto.convertiPunto1: It finds the repeating tile on its own, even when the rows are offset as in brickwork.
prodotto.convertiPunto2: How many colours to keep is your decision, and you watch the result change as you decide.
prodotto.convertiPunto3: It tells you how much the reconstruction matches the original, and shows you where it is wrong.
prodotto.convertiNota: PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, BMP. It works better on flat drawings than on photographs: continuous shading is something no flat fill can render.
